keeping in touch st mary’s parish, bennekerry 25th october 2026 thirtieth sunday in ordinary time the falling of the leaves autumn is over the long leaves that love us, and over the mice in the barley sheaves. yellow the leaves of the rowan above us, and yellow the wet wild-strawberry leaves. the hour of the waning of love has beset us, and weary and worn are our sad souls now. let us the season of passion forget us, with a kiss and a tear on thy drooping brow. william butler yeats next weekend: feast of all saints and feast of all souls mass with commemoration of the faithful departed bennekerry church: sunday 1st november at 11.30am commemoration of the faithful departed mass in askea church: monday 2nd november 2026 at 7pm

for more information or see pambutleryoga.com/shop for booking details. graiguecullen bingo: tuesday 27th october 2026 in st. fiacc’s hall 8.30pm. jackpot on 40 numbers € 700. double number € 320. lotto € 3 400. bonus ball € 2 700 k&l reading group: our kildare & leighlin reading group takes place on wednesday, 4th november 2026 from 3.30 pm – 5.pm in st. patricks/ carlow college. the focus of our discussion will be on the challenge of a. i. members are asked to read the article and will be invited to respond to it at our meeting. the group normally meets three times a year, with our meeting and tea/coffee hosted in the college by conn ó maoldhomhnaigh. all are most welcome. if anyone would like to receive a copy of the article, please contact fr. paul or fr. conn. carlow flower club: our october/halloween demonstration is by diane gallagher aoifa, teacher judge and demonstrator from doddervale flower club, tuesday 27th october at 8 pm woodford dolmen hotel. all arrangements will be raffled on the night. competition for all classes will be “autumn fruits & berries” a table arrangement. visitors welcome, visitors fee €10. there will be a plant sale on the night. holy family askea: is open for enrolments for the 2027/2028 school year from 16th october 2026 to 6th november 2026. application forms are available to download at:

or in person at holy family askea, carlow, r93 vx27 barrow valley art group: annual exhibition of paintings, in association with carlow county hospice, will be held in cobden hall, st patrick’s college carlow from saturday 24th to saturday 31st october. exhibition open sunday 25th 11 am to 5 pm, monday to friday 11 am to 5 pm, and saturday 31st - 11 am to 1 pm. all welcome, admission free.

sacred music workshop day for parish choirs – calling all choir members. bishop denis and the commission for liturgical formation are hosting a workshop day for choir members in the diocese on saturday, 21 november 2026 from 11-4:30 in carlow cathedral. led by marian gaynor and team. this promises to be a lovely day for choir members with a music pack, the diocesan guide for music ministry, a hot lunch and a big sing of liam lawton’s ‘magnificat’ all included. the day is free of charge, but places are limited and registration is essential. music pack and lunch can only be provided for choir members from the diocese who have booked a place. bookings open on monday 19 october. the irish cancer society is seeking compassionate volunteer drivers: as a volunteer driver you would be bringing patients undergoing chemotherapy to the hospital and back home for their treatment. gifting your time means that cancer patients will have comfortable (one on one) transport to attend appointments for their lifesaving treatment. if you can spare 2 days per month, have a valid driving licence, a nd a safe, reliable vehicle, you are the perfect candidate to make a significant difference. the irish cancer society will provide you with training before you start as a driver for us. your generosity not only eases the journey for many during a challenging time but also offers comfort and support when it's needed most. for more information and to become a volunteer driver, please contact monica or emily at
volunteer@irishcancer.ie

synodal pathway update: national synodal assembly: saturday, 17th october, was a momentous and historic day in the life of the irish church in which over a dozen delegates from our diocese participated. locally in our parishes there is much to receive from the prayer, listening and discernment of the past five years. the working document for the assembly is still a valuable document for parishes and a number of accounts and reports from the day can be viewed in the latest news section of
these are important to read alongside the raw figures on each proposal. our delegates will gather with bishop denis on 3rd november to reflect on the assembly and where it is leads us now.

calendar 27th october: st otteran, a descendant of conall gulban, is usually identified with odhran who preceded colum cille in iona. his death is recorded in 548 and his grave was greatly revered in iona. he was chosen by the vikings as patron of the city of waterford in 1096 and later patron of the diocese. 28th october: saints simon and jude. the teaching of the apostles is the living gospel for all to hear. their authority comes from their fidelity to christ and his message. we pray today that they continue to watch over the church and give protection against error. st jude is patron of hopeless causes. 29th october: st colman hailed from kilmacduagh, co. galway, in the 7th century after studying in aran, where he founded two churches on inis mhór, he returned to make a foundation at kilmacduagh. 31st october blessed dominic collins was born around 1566 in youghall co. cork. in 1598, after a military career, he entered the society of jesus as a brother. he returned to ireland in 1601, but on 17 june 1601 he was captured by the english who tried in vain to make him renounce his faith. he was hanged in his native city on 31 october 1602.
